data.title: Eli Lilly Stock (LLY) Has 45% Upside, Says Citigroup
data.description:
Citigroup (C) has placed a new Street-high price target on Eli Lilly's (LLY) stock and sees 45% upside in the shares. Geoff Meacham, a five-star rated analyst with a 59% success rate, has placed a $1,600 price target on LLY stock, the highest on Wall Street. The price target from the Citigroup analyst is 45% higher than where Eli Lilly's shares currently trade.

Meacham also reiterated his Buy rating on LLY stock. In a note to clients, he said that Eli Lilly is the global leader in weight-loss drugs with a 60% market share. Eli Lilly's weight-loss and diabetes drugs are now doing $14.9 billion in combined quarterly sales, notes the analyst. Meacham also praised Eli Lilly for being a diversified pharmaceutical company with more than 40 active phase three clinical trials underway related to illnesses such as cancer, immunology and neuroscience.

Novo Nordisk Rebrands

In his note, Meacham highlights that Eli Lilly's stock has dropped 8% over the past month, presenting a buying opportunity to investors. The bullish note on LLY stock from Citigroup comes as rival pharmaceutical company Novo Nordisk (NVO) announced that it is rebranding. Going forward, the Danish company will be known simply as "Novo."

data.title: Ford Stock (NYSE:F) Slips With News of 223,000 Recalled Vehicles
data.description:
Legacy automaker Ford (F) has been trying diligently to shake concerns about quality in its vehicles, and on many fronts, it succeeded. But it also finds itself in contention with a growing list of recalls. Today, another nearly 223,000 vehicles found themselves subject to recall, and over issues with the fuel tank. The news did not sit well with investors, and Ford shares dropped fractionally in Monday afternoon's trading. Ford has also seen a 19.61% rally in its share price over the past year.

A Pretty Important Recall, Too

The roughly 223,000 vehicles subject to recall here are being recalled over issues with the fuel tank, according to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA). The tank may be "improperly secured," which in turn can cause the tank to "…leak fuel, or detach from the vehicle while driving." Such an issue can also "…cause an engine stall or increase the risk of fire."

Apparently, the fuel tank straps may have been improperly assembled, which could cause the leaks or outright detachment. Moreover, the only vehicles impacted by this are Ford F-150 models made between 2023 and 2027, which are some of Ford's biggest sellers. As ever, dealerships will take over on the front lines here, inspecting tank straps and replacing them where necessary.

A Push-to-Move Experience

Car and Driver, meanwhile, brought word of a new patent out of Ford that could have unexpected results. The patent describes a new way to move a truck very, very small distances by simply pushing it. For anyone who has ever hauled a load, and needed the load to be dropped in a very specific place, such a patent could represent a big help.

The patent is called "systems and methods for moving a vehicle using externally mounted HMI." Using the pop-up grab handle included on F-series trucks, the user would be able to effectively "nudge" the vehicle small distances with the grab handle. The movement right now seems limited to forward and reverse only, however. Such a system could be particularly useful in parking spaces; how often have you ever wished you could move just a little further into a space without restarting the car?

data.title: AI Will Be "Bigger than Oil, Gold, Diamonds, or even the Internet," Trump Says
data.description:
President Trump brushed aside warnings from OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, arguing that AI development in the U.S. should continue to accelerate at a fast pace. "AI, and Data Centers, will be the Greatest Economic Development Engine in History ­­— Bigger than Oil, Gold, Diamonds, or even the Internet," Trump said in a Truth Social post on Monday.

Over the weekend, both Altman and Amodei warned that AI could lead to destructive outcomes if proper safeguards aren't put in place.

Trump Pushes Ahead on AI, Criticizes Permitting Delays

Trump added that advancements in AI won't be stopped by "Destructive Forces" during his term. In a separate post, he attributed backlash against AI and data centers to U.S. dominance in the sector.

data.title: Costco Stock (COST) in Focus as Company Limits Motor Oil Purchases
data.description:
Costco Wholesale (COST) has raised prices and begun to limit purchases of motor oil sold at its U.S. stores as lubricant supplies tighten. The warehouse club has raised the price of its Kirkland Signature full-synthetic motor oil and introduced purchase limits. The 10-quart package sold at Costco, which contains two five-quart bottles, now sells for $57.99, nearly double its previous price of $30.

At the same time, customers of Costco are being limited to two packages of the motor oil per week, with some locations setting a limit of one purchase at a time. Costco has also imposed limits on the Mobil 1 full-synthetic six-quart packs of motor oil that it sells in the U.S., with the price for that product now set at $44.

Rising Oil Prices Hit Costco

Other major sellers of motor oil such as Walmart (WMT), Amazon (AMZN), and AutoZone (AZO) do not appear to have followed Costco (COST) yet in significantly hiking motor oil prices or limiting purchases.

data.title: Dow Jones: DJIA Dips on AI Development Warnings as Rate Hike Odds Advance
data.description:
The Dow Jones (DJIA) is down 0.12% on Monday after OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei voiced concerns about the speed of AI advancements. In an X post, Altman cautioned that humanity "could lose control of the future to AI" without proper safeguards. Furthermore, he said a concentration of AI under one person or company could lead to an "extremely dystopian" outcome.

Meanwhile, Amodei warned in a 3,800-word essay that developing AI irresponsibly could cause economic disruption and more cybersecurity attacks. "We must slow the pace at which we improve the capabilities of AI models," he wrote.

President Trump downplayed the concerns of the two leaders, arguing that the only guardrails necessary are a "STRONG AND SMART (High IQ!) PRESIDENT, and the U.S.A. has that, in spades!" Over the weekend, he cautioned that slowing down the pace of AI could cause China to overtake the U.S. in the industry.

data.title: Boeing Stock (NYSE:BA) Notches Up, SPEEA Contract Deal Looks Close
data.description:
Recently, we heard about aerospace stock Boeing (BA) and its move to restart negotiations again with the Society of Professional Engineering Employees in Aerospace (SPEEA). The first move ended with SPEEA rejecting the contract rather heavily, and so, Boeing made another offer. It was Boeing's final offer, noted a report from Fox 13 in Seattle, and it seems to have done the job. Boeing shares ticked up fractionally in Monday afternoon's trading. Boeing has seen a 2.46% loss in its share price over the past year.

It Just Might Be Over

SPEEA's leadership recommended approval of the deal, which Boeing called its "final contract offer" according to Fox 13. The new contract offer calls for a guaranteed 10% wage hike after the contract is approved, and another 4% increase to kick in starting with March 2027. There were also revisions to some of the language on work-from-home policies, as well as overtime limits for some parts of the union. A set of "wage pools" was also established for the three years following the 2027 raises.

Boeing's vice president and functional chief engineer for Production Engineering, Ben Nimmergut, noted, "Our final contract offer addresses the top priorities identified by our employees and SPEEA's bargaining teams, including an immediate wage increase and larger wage pools with guarantees. We're optimistic this will allow all of us to focus on the important work ahead."

data.title: Google Stock (GOOGL) Pops 3% as Company Plans to Build an AI Data Center in New Mexico
data.description:
The stock of Google's parent company Alphabet (GOOGL) is up 3% on reports that company is planning to build an artificial intelligence (AI) data center in New Mexico. Multiple media reports say that Alphabet is considering building a new large-scale data center in Lea County, New Mexico, and is focused on community outreach as a key part of the project's development.

"Our goal in Lea County is simple: serve as long-term partners who can be counted on to do the right thing in support of the places we call home," said Alphabet said in a blog post about the proposed project. "That includes responsibly managing vital water resources, paying for 100% of the energy we use and infrastructure we need, and showing up as active members of the community."

An AI Slowdown?

News that Alphabet is planning a new data center that will potentially cost billions of dollar to build and operate comes on the day when Wall Street is trying assess whether companies will slow their progress on developing AI technologies. In recent days, Dario Amodei, the CEO of AI startup Anthropic has called for a slowdown in developing the technology, and OpenAI announced that it is canceling its planned initial public offering (IPO) that had been planned for this year.

data.title: Why Are Gold and Silver Down Today, 9/14/26?
data.description:
Both gold (XAUUSD) and silver (XAGUSD) are trading lower on Monday. Over the past 24 hours, gold and silver are down 0.76% and 1.24%, respectively. The two precious metals have faced pressure in recent days due to higher interest rate expectations and elevated Treasury yields.

Rate hike expectations at the Fed interest rate decision on September 16 continue to rise as inflation remains stubborn and above the Fed's 2% target. The odds of a 25-basis-point hike later this week are at 91.1%, up from 87.3% on Friday and 59.4% a week ago, according to the CME FedWatch tool.

High Yields Reduce Appeal of Precious Metals

Higher rates are typically viewed as a negative for gold and silver. As rates rise, the opportunity cost of holding precious metals increases relative to interest-bearing assets such as Treasuries.
